clue.text: It's an easy thing to acquire

definitions.text: It's an easy thing to acquire

parts.words: It's an easy thing to acquire
parts.note: reads as something cheaply obtained, but describes a skill or ease of doing that one picks up

explanation.surface: Something that can be picked up without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to describe a bargain, but it describes a knack: an easy manner or aptitude that a person acquires.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ease or aptitude in doing something, a talent that can be gained.

clue.text: Season for a Transatlantic trip?

definitions.meaning: the American name for autumn, the season as a Transatlantic speaker calls it
to trip is to stumble and tumble over

explanation.surface: Which time of year suits a voyage across the Atlantic?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transatlantic' here stands for an American, whose word for autumn is the answer; 'trip' is not a journey but a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call autumn by this name, and a stumble or tumble is also called this.

clue.text: Bloke much sought after by Ted

definitions.meaning: old slang for a chap or fellow
a sheltered little bay, a spot an ordinary holidaying chap called Ted would hunt for

explanation.surface: A fellow whom someone named Ted is eager to find.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the small sheltered bay on a coastline, which a holidaymaker (Ted, an everyday name) goes looking for.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls a fellow this, and a sheltered inlet of the coast is a favourite seaside goal.

clue.text: Homer's country ?

parts.note: the saying 'even Homer nods' means the great poet sometimes dozed, so his country is the realm of sleep

explanation.surface: Which land was the epic poet's home?
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a question about Greece, but the proverb 'even Homer sometimes nods' sends him to the biblical region whose name became a joke for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical region east of Eden became an idiom for sleep, and the proverb has Homer nodding off.

clue.text: Snare a confused parent

indicators.note: a confused parent is one jumbled up, so the letters of the word are mixed

explanation.surface: Catching out a muddled mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is an old word meaning to trap or ensnare someone.

clue.text: Betting men lose a hundred and still have plenty of dough

definitions.note: a plural phrase meaning people who keep lots of dough

indicators.note: the betting men lose something, so it is taken out of their word

parts.note: backers are people who put money on a horse
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Punters drop a hundred pounds but remain well off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' looks like slang for money, which suits gamblers, but it is the real bread dough in a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread makers work with dough all day, so they always have a supply of it.

clue.text: Spirit kept a dozen years in wood

definitions.text: Spirit kept a dozen years in wood

parts.words: Spirit kept a dozen years in wood
parts.note: sounds like whisky aged twelve years in a cask, but recalls the sprite in The Tempest imprisoned in a cloven pine

explanation.surface: A twelve-year-old whisky matured in a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' and 'kept in wood' suggest cask-aged liquor; in Shakespeare's The Tempest the witch Sycorax shut this sprite in a split pine for twelve years.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's airy sprite was trapped in a pine tree for twelve years before Prospero freed him.

clue.text: Their favourites are likely to get cross

definitions.text: Their favourites are likely to get cross

parts.words: Their favourites are likely to get cross
parts.note: a cross is the mark put on a ballot paper beside a chosen candidate

explanation.surface: People whose darlings tend to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' seems to mean angry, but it is the X a voter marks against the candidate they favour.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of voters marks a cross beside the candidates they prefer.

clue.text: Part estate in the North Country

definitions.note: a place found in the north of England

parts.note: to part is to separate or sunder
an estate is landed property, land

explanation.surface: A portion of a property located up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'North Country' is the North of England, where this town stands on the River Wear.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a port town in north-east England, on the River Wear.

clue.text: Hill of old world fragrance

definitions.meaning: ... Hill is a well-known street in Battersea, south London
a sweet old-fashioned scent from a purple-flowered herb

explanation.surface: A slope with an old-fashioned perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense depends on knowing the London street name Lavender Hill, in Battersea.
explanation.definitionFit: A London street is called this ___ Hill, and the herb's scent is a traditional perfume.

clue.text: One dig upset the judge

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A single jab overturned the verdict of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: The judge is not a courtroom one but one of the Judges of Israel in the Old Testament, who led the defeat of the Midianites.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the leaders in the Book of Judges in the Bible.

clue.text: Room where loans can be arranged

indicators.note: letters that can be arranged are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An office where a bank's loans are set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing room or reception room, especially one for entertaining guests.

clue.text: Boy engaged on a piece of music

parts.note: a boy is a son
at, as in 'at work' meaning busy with a task

explanation.surface: A lad occupied in learning a musical composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical composition in several movements, usually for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Haunted by memories ? Try the river

definitions.text: Haunted by memories ? Try the river

parts.words: Haunted by memories ? Try the river
parts.note: in Greek myth one river of the underworld made those who drank from it forget everything

explanation.surface: Advice to someone troubled by the past: go and drown sorrows.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like grim advice to jump in a river; the river meant is the one in Hades whose water brings forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of oblivion in Hades, whose waters wiped the drinker's memory.

clue.text: Material for a best suit

parts.note: reads as tailoring cloth, but means the cards of the suit that wins tricks in a card game

explanation.surface: Cloth for one's Sunday clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' and 'material' point to a tailor; in card games the best suit is the one named trumps, whose cards beat all others.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards of the ruling suit outrank every other card, making it the best suit.

clue.text: How to show complete disdain

parts.note: an adverb saying in what way contempt is shown; split as scorn and fully it also says to scorn completely

explanation.surface: Instructions for expressing total contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray apostrophe after 'complete'; the page has none. Split into two words the answer itself says 'disdain completely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with contempt and derision is acting in this way.

clue.text: The dramatist with a nicer disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A playwright of a kinder temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' seems to mean temperament, but it is its other sense, arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a great seventeenth-century French tragic playwright.

clue.text: Poor Carl is in rank disorder

indicators.note: disorder means a muddle, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An unfortunate man named Carl is in a terrible mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank disorder' reads as utter chaos; 'rank' is the definition, a military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned army rank, above lance-corporal and below sergeant.

clue.text: There's no object in love for tennis

definitions.text: There's no object in love for tennis

parts.words: There's no object in love for tennis
parts.note: in tennis, love is the score of zero; a score of nothing has no points, and no object means no purpose

explanation.surface: A remark that romance has no purpose for a tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' seems romantic but is tennis's zero score; having no point is also having no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Without purpose and without any score, as love is in tennis.

clue.text: Look hard around you-sound material here

indicators.note: the word for looking hard goes around the next piece

parts.note: to look hard is to gaze

indicators.note: sound tells us to take the way the word you is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: the word you, said out loud, is the letter U

explanation.surface: Stare closely at what surrounds you, material that is sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You-sound' asks for the letter that is said like 'you', namely U, which goes inside GAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, open-weave fabric is a kind of material.

clue.text: A circle of twelve

definitions.meaning: a great circle of the earth passing through both poles

explanation.surface: A round of twelve things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' is the hour of noon, an old sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a line of longitude around the globe and, in old usage, the noon hour.

clue.text: Final metamorphosis of the Red Queen

definitions.text: Final metamorphosis of the Red Queen

parts.words: Final metamorphosis of the Red Queen
parts.note: at the end of Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen Alice shakes turns into her pet cat's young one

explanation.surface: The last transformation of a chess queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, Alice shakes the Red Queen and she becomes Kitty, Alice's young black cat.
explanation.definitionFit: In the story the chess queen changes into Alice's young pet cat.

clue.text: By rotation, transpose it and retire

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase for retire swap places

parts.note: to retire to bed is to turn in

explanation.surface: Taking turns, switch it round and go to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points to the phrase for 'retire', TURN IN, whose two words change places.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things by rotation is doing them one after another, each in sequence.

clue.text: Blows at arm's-length

definitions.meaning: the ends of shirt sleeves at the wrists, the far end of the arm

explanation.surface: Punches thrown from a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At arm's-length' sounds like keeping someone away, but means the very end of the arm, where sleeve ends are.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaps are called this, and so are the turned-back ends of sleeves at the wrist.

clue.text: Does he belong to the vegetable kingdom ?

definitions.text: Does he belong to the vegetable kingdom ?

parts.words: Does he belong to the vegetable kingdom ?
parts.note: a man from ... shares his name with a root vegetable

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kingdom' suggests the plant kingdom, but also a monarchy: a native of the kingdom of Sweden shares his name with a turnip-like root.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Sweden shares the name of a yellow-fleshed root vegetable.

clue.text: "Dropt from the like a falling star " (Milton)

definitions.text: "Dropt from the like a falling star " (Milton)

parts.words: "Dropt from the like a falling star " (Milton)
parts.note: a gap in a line of Paradise Lost about the fall of the builder-angel Mulciber, to be filled with the missing word

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash where the missing word goes; in Paradise Lost the angel is 'Dropt from the ___ like a falling star', that is, from the top of the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of the heavens, directly overhead, from which the angel falls.

clue.text: Bound to have varied diet

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Obliged to eat a range of foods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to'; 'Bound' alone is the definition, meaning fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound is fastened or knotted up.

clue.text: Old pen for raising stags

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: stags are male deer

explanation.surface: An ancient enclosure for rearing male deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' seems to be an enclosure for animals, but it is a writing pen cut from a stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Early writing pens were cut from the hollow stems of marsh grasses.

clue.text: Francisco gave much thanks for it

definitions.text: Francisco gave much thanks for it

parts.words: Francisco gave much thanks for it
parts.note: in the opening scene of Hamlet the sentry Francisco, handed over from duty, says 'For this ___ much thanks'

explanation.surface: Someone named Francisco was very grateful for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Francisco is the sentry at the start of Hamlet; when Bernardo comes to take over the watch he says 'For this ___ much thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken off sentry duty by the next guard is being granted this.

clue.text: It's merely childish

parts.note: describes behaviour fit for a youngster, immature

explanation.surface: Dismissing something as silly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes young people and immature, childlike behaviour.

clue.text: Conducted beyond the piggery, so called

indicators.note: the word for conducted comes after the piggery, further along

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
conducted means led

explanation.surface: Escorted past the pigsty, as it is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Something named or designated in a particular way is so called.

clue.text: Partial — like the club with no reserve team ?

definitions.text: like the club with no reserve team ?
definitions.meaning: a club fielding only its first team has just a single eleven

explanation.surface: A biased remark about a club with no second string.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer literally: a club with no reserves puts out one team only.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased judgement is unfair, and a club with only one team fields a single side.
